thread:
infra-bot: ALERT: unusual Xid error rate detected on cluster us-west2-gpu-pool (Xid 13 spike). 15 distinct GPUs flagged in last 30m. https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/3821
maria_gpuops: Looking now - grouping by Xid code. seeing 13, 31, and a couple 48s. counts per node attached in a sec.
ben_sre: When did this start? Any rolling deploys or config changes? Could be a driver/kernel regression.
raj_serving: No deploys scheduled for that fleet. High traffic from gen-heavy pods 10:10-10:40; lots of long-seq chat completions (seq_len ~ 3k) with batch_size 48-64.
maria_gpuops: quick snapshot from telemetry:

```
# sample from node gpu-uw2-17
Timestamp: 2026-04-10T10:37:12Z
Xid Errors: Xid13=7, Xid31=2, Xid48=1
ECC Corrected: 12
ECC Uncorrected: 0
Driver: 535.86.01
CUDA: 12.2
```

maria_gpuops: Xid13 is highest and concentrated on cards with elevated corrected ECC counts but not necessarily uncorrected.
chandra_hw: historically we've seen Xid13 correlated with memory/page faults under heavy KV cache usage or long sequences where allocation pressure spikes.
ben_sre: Any pattern by workload type? batch vs streaming? pinned vs mapped allocator?
raj_serving: It's mostly batched generation runs (many parallel requests batched by runtime), not streaming. Runtime uses mmap-weighted tokenizer cache and pre-allocated KV cache pools.
maria_gpuops: Correlation matrix I just ran (quick and noisy):
- Xid13 spikes <-> high batch_size + long seq_len (rho ~0.48)
- Xid31 spikes <-> frequent short jobs with many context switches (rho ~0.35)
- Xid48 occurrences near nodes with intermittent PCIe errors in dmesg

ben_sre: Good. Any thermal or power anomalies in sensors? Could be overheating or PSU hiccups causing PCIe resets.
chandra_hw: Temps look fine. I/O lane errors in lspci show occasional AER logs on two cards.
maria_gpuops: dmesg excerpt from gpu-uw2-17:

```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (13): PID 4821     Graphics Exception: ESR 0x00000004
[  123.456790] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  123.456791] pcieport 0000:62:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: rx err
```

raj_serving: "GPU has fallen off the bus" usually means PCIe reset - that matches Xid48-ish behaviour too.
ben_sre: For triage, propose:
1) Immediately cordon and drain nodes with >5 Xid13 in last 24h into maintenance pool (avoid mass eviction during peak hours).
2) Capture a reproducer: run isolated long-seq batched generator on suspect card with env LOG_LEVEL=debug and nvprof traces.
3) Collect full kernel/journal, nvml logs, firmware versions, AER counts and link to ticket.
4) If hardware shows repeated AERs or "fallen off the bus" - schedule replace under warranty.

maria_gpuops: Agreed. I'll start a small job to reproduce on gpu-uw2-17 and gpu-uw2-22 (both top offenders). Will reduce batch_size to 16 and then step up to 64 to confirm threshold.
chandra_hw: Also check BIOS/PCIe link speed and power capping. Some cards revert to Gen1 on bad cables.
raj_serving: Quick mitigation if reproducer confirms: reduce default batch_size for that pool to 32 and enable KV prefetch throttling to reduce peak allocator pressure.
ben_sre: Firmware/driver plan: pin to last-known-good driver (535.54.x) on a canary node and rerun repro. If it stabilizes, roll back cluster-wide after QA.
maria_gpuops: Action list I'll own:
- [ ] run repro on two suspect nodes (start in 10m)
- [ ] collect nvml dump, dmesg, journal, driver info and attach to ticket INFRA-987
- [ ] add Xid->workload mapping to our telemetry (tag generation job IDs)

raj_serving: I'll change runtime batching policy for us-west2 pool to conservative mode for next 6 hours :gear: 
ben_sre: I'll coordinate maintenance window with platform and open a hardware ticket for cards with persistent AERs.
chandra_hw: If replacement required, test new cards for >24h under stress before putting back into production.
infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-987 and scheduled maintenance: 2026-04-10T22:00Z-23:00Z for targeted node replacements. https://redwood/infra/INFRA-987
maria_gpuops: repro started. initial run: batch_size=16, seq=2048 - no Xid in 12m. stepping to batch_size=48 now.
maria_gpuops: 3m into batch_size=48 run -> Xid13 at 10:55 on gpu-uw2-17. capturing traces.
ben_sre: ok that's consistent. Mark node for immediate drain after current pods finish. Leave one canary node until repro/driver test is done.
raj_serving: switched runtime to conservative batching. rolling update applied.
maria_gpuops: attaching probe commands for future triage:

```
# collect NVML and driver state
nvidia-smi -q -a > /tmp/nv_q.txt
sudo dmesg | egrep -i "nvrm|xid|aer|gpu has fallen off" > /tmp/dmesg_xid.txt
nv-hostengine --show-all
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
```

ben_sre: One more note - add a Grafana panel that overlays Xid rates with 95th percentile latency and batch_size distribution. That should make root-cause faster.
maria_gpuops: Good ask. I'll add it to the dashboard INFRA-987-DB.
raj_serving: Thx team. Keep updates in INFRA-987 and drop short summaries here. :thumbsup: 
maria_gpuops: will do. current status -> repro confirmed for high batch+long-seq; mitigations in place; maintenance scheduled. Closing here after hardware ticket created.
